mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 350 petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 (2004-2010) has the well-documented balance shaft sprocket failure - a serious issue affecting early production units. The M276 (2011-2018) is more reliable but suffers from timing chain tensioner and NOx sensor issues. M272 balance shaft failure affects pre-2008 engines - check engine serial number. Fault codes P0016/P0017 indicate timing correlation issues. M276 timing chain rattle on cold start can indicate tensioner wear. NOx sensor replacement is a common maintenance item on M276 engines. 2008+ M272 and all M276 engines have improved components.

mainEntity.name: What is the M272 balance shaft problem on the Mercedes CLS 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 V6 engine has a balance shaft sprocket made from inadequately hardened steel on early production units. As the sprocket teeth wear, the timing chain becomes slack, causing incorrect camshaft timing [2†L7-L10][2†L18-L21]. Affects CLS 350 (2004-2008, M272 engines below serial #468993) [13†L41-L42]. Symptoms: check engine light with P0016/P0017 codes, rattling on startup. Repair is engine-out and labour-intensive - £2,500-£3,800 at a specialist [13†L5-L6]. 2008+ facelift engines have hardened sprockets and are safe. Warning: Ignoring the rattle and codes can lead to timing chain jumping, valve damage, and complete engine destruction.

mainEntity.name: What causes loss of power on my Mercedes CLS 350 with no warning lights?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common culprits include NOx sensor failure (M276 engines), carbon buildup on intake valves due to direct injection, or failing ignition coils. NOx sensors can fail without storing permanent codes. Carbon cleaning may be required every 50,000-80,000 miles on direct-injection M276 engines. Check VIN online to confirm if your engine is in the affected balance shaft range. Ignition coil and spark plug condition can also cause power loss.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 500 M278 V8 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M278 is a powerful and rewarding engine, but it has serious potential weaknesses. Timing chain tensioner failure and cylinder wall scoring are the main concerns. Timing chain rattle on cold start is common - don't ignore it. Cylinder wall scoring can cause high oil consumption and eventual engine failure [3†L6-L7]. Have cylinders bore scoped if oil consumption is excessive [16†L6-L8]. Oil leaks from cam sensor covers are common but not catastrophic. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLS 350/500 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained M272 V6 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. M276 engines are newer but expected to achieve similar mileage. M278 V8s can also reach high mileage, but timing chain and cylinder scoring issues can occur earlier. M272: 150k-200k+ miles with regular servicing. M276: 150k+ miles with NOx sensors as the main maintenance item. M278: 100k-150k+ miles if timing chain and cylinder scoring are addressed. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CLS 350 and CLS 500 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CLS 350 uses a 3.5-litre V6 (M272 or M276) producing 272-306 hp, while the CLS 500 uses a 4.7-5.0-litre V8 (M113 or M278) producing 306-408+ hp. The CLS 500 offers significantly more performance but higher running costs. CLS 350 (M272/M276): 272-306 hp, V6, smoother and more economical. CLS 500 (M113/M278): 306-408+ hp, V8, more power and torque. M278 twin-turbo (2011+) delivers 408 hp and 600 Nm torque. Both are available with 4MATIC all-wheel drive on later models.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLS 350/500 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLS 350 and CLS 500 represent the petrol-powered soul of the CLS range. The CLS 350 debuted in 2004 with the M272 3.5-litre V6, later receiving the M276 direct-injection V6 in the C218 generation. The CLS 500 arrived with a naturally aspirated 5.0-litre M113 V8 in 2004, before being replaced by the M278 4.7-litre twin-turbo V8 in 2011. Together, these engines spanned three generations and over a decade of four-door coupé motoring.

milestones.description: CLS 350 launched with M272 E35 3.5L V6, 272 hp, 350 Nm, 7G-TRONIC
CLS 500 launched with M113 E50 5.0L V8, 306 hp, 460 Nm, 7G-TRONIC
CLS 350 CGI introduced with direct-injection M272, 288 hp
C218 CLS 350 launched with M276 DE35 3.5L V6, 306 hp, 370 Nm, 7G-TRONIC PLUS
CLS 500 replaced by M278 DEH46 LA 4.7L twin-turbo V8, 408 hp, 600 Nm
C218 facelift: 9G-TRONIC introduced; CLS 500 gains 449 hp in some markets
C257 CLS 350 moves to M264 2.0L four-cylinder MHEV (not covered here)
CLS 500 discontinued; replaced by CLS 450/53 AMG MHEV

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLS 350/500 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLS 350 and CLS 500 are powered by some of Mercedes' most celebrated petrol engines - the M272 and M276 V6s, and the M278 twin-turbo V8. However, each has its own well-documented weaknesses. The M272 is infamous for balance shaft sprocket failure, while the M276 suffers from timing chain tensioner and NOx sensor issues. The M278 twin-turbo V8 can develop timing chain rattle, cylinder wall scoring, and oil leaks. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.group: M272 Balance Shaft & Timing Chain Failure
problems.h4: M272 Balance Shaft & Timing Chain Failure - The CLS 350's Defining Weakness
problems.rootCause: The balance shaft sprocket was manufactured with inadequate heat treatment on early production units, causing the teeth to wear prematurely. As the teeth wear, the timing chain becomes slack, leading to incorrect camshaft timing. The engine may run poorly, trigger fault codes P0016/P0017, and in severe cases, the chain can jump and cause catastrophic valve/piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace balance shaft sprocket with hardened unit, timing chain, tensioners, guides. Engine-out job on most models
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles if caught before catastrophic failure; the only reliable repair

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt M272 with upgraded timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if timing has jumped and valve damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: The balance shaft issue is the single most significant problem affecting the M272 engine. If you own a pre-2008 CLS 350, check the engine serial number - units below 2729..30 468993 are in the affected range. If you have fault codes P0016/P0017 or rattling on startup, don't delay - specialist repair at £2,500-£3,800 is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. For cars with high mileage or other issues, a rebuilt unit with upgraded sprockets offers peace of mind.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M272 Mercedes CLS 350 engine prices

problems.group: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner & NOx Sensor Issues
problems.h4: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner & NOx Sensor Issues - CLS 350 (2011-2018)
problems.rootCause: The M276 timing chain tensioners rely on oil pressure to maintain chain tension. When the engine is stood for a period, oil can drain from the tensioners, causing a brief rattling noise on cold start. This is often harmless if brief, but persistent rattle indicates wear. NOx sensors are a common failure point on M276 engines, with some owners reporting repeated replacements.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; brief cold start rattle only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if persistent rattle or chain stretch is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M276 with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped and valves have contacted pistons

problems.recommendation: The M276 is generally more reliable than the M272, but timing chain tensioner wear is a known issue. A brief rattle on cold start (1-2 seconds) is often normal, but persistent rattle requires attention. NOx sensor replacement is a common maintenance item on these engines - budget for it if you're buying a higher-mileage CLS 350.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M276 timing chain repair for your Mercedes CLS 350

problems.group: M278 Timing Chain Rattle & Cylinder Scoring
problems.h4: M278 Timing Chain Rattle & Cylinder Scoring - CLS 500 V8 Weaknesses
problems.rootCause: Early M278 V8s suffer from timing chain tensioner problems causing a "bag of nails" rattle on cold start. More seriously, cylinder wall scoring has been reported in some units, leading to high oil consumption and eventual engine failure. Oil leaks from cam sensor covers are also common.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; cold start rattle only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, guides and sprockets. Engine-out job
repairOptions.longevity: Required if persistent rattle or chain stretch is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine strip, cylinder honing or sleeving, new piston rings
repairOptions.longevity: Required if scoring is detected; expensive but cheaper than replacement

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M278 with upgraded timing components and cylinder work, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if scoring is severe or bottom-end damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: The M278 is a powerful and rewarding engine, but it has serious potential weaknesses. If you hear rattling on cold start, get the timing chain tensioners inspected immediately. More critically, if the engine is consuming oil, have the cylinders bore scoped to check for scoring - this is the most significant failure risk on the M278. A rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components and cylinder work is the only safe option if scoring is detected.
